releaseNotes: Six copies of escapeHtml are now one, in scripts/lib/html.ts. The copies lived in three renderers (render-launch-cockpit, render-design-room, lib/render-artifact-page), one shared markup builder (lib/founder-gate-presentation), one gate that asserts against rendered output (check-founder-operator-bootstrap), and one machine report writer (refresh-source-freshness). They had already drifted into two shapes: three took `string` and three took `unknown`. That split is the interesting part, because check-founder-operator-bootstrap grades the very HTML render-launch-cockpit produces, and the two disagreed about what an absent value escapes to — the gate would have escaped `undefined` to a thrown TypeError while the renderer escaped it to the literal text "undefined". Neither behaviour is right and nothing was pinning either one.

The shared signature is the wider of the two. `String(value ?? "")` is the identity on a string, so the three former `string` callers are byte-for-byte unchanged, and a nullish value now renders as an empty cell in every caller rather than differing by which copy it reached. render:launch-cockpit and render:design-room both re-render identically, and check:generated-pages still byte-matches every authored-from page against a fresh render.

The single quote is still deliberately not escaped, and the shared file says why so the next reader does not helpfully add it. Every attribute this skill writes is double-quoted, so `'` needs no escaping to be safe; escaping it would rewrite the bytes of every generated page, which check:generated-pages compares against a fresh render and which design-room.html pins as a byte-identical static fallback. A stricter escape buys nothing here and turns two byte-match gates red.

business/resend/email-templates.ts keeps its own copy on purpose and is not a seventh caller. It is payload copied into a launched business repo, where nothing under scripts/ exists to import, and its extra `'` rule is correct for its own reason: email HTML passes through client rewriters that do not all agree on attribute quoting. A comment now records both halves of that, because the file otherwise reads as the one that was missed.

lib/render-artifact-page.ts carried a comment saying its copy was duplicated deliberately and that collapsing all four into one helper was "a real cleanup and a separate review". This is that review, and the count in the comment was low — the file named three siblings when there were five. The comment is gone rather than corrected; a note explaining why a duplicate exists outlives its usefulness the moment the duplicate does.
